newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos appealed to the Malaysian government and businessmen not to let the Manila Hotel ruling cloud their view of otherwise attractive investment opportunities in the country. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Hong Kong's future chief executive Tung Chee-hwa promised to look after the welfare of the territory's 140,000 Filipinos, mostly domestic helpers, after the handover on July 1. (BULLETIN)
- The Department of Justice created a panel of prosecutors to conduct preliminary investigations into accusations that tycoon Lucio Tan had evaded 25.6 billion pesos in taxes. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co has reduced by almost 30 percent the number of telephone lines it will install this year to 308,000 from 400,000 due to a shift in company priorities toward the improvement of its present massive telephone network. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The National Power Corp sees its selling rates doubling to five pesos per kilowatt-hour in the next eight years, if it postpones the planned sale of its operations and assets this year. (BULLETIN)
- The Energy Industry Administration Board has stepped up its monitoring of the prices of petroleum products as the deregulation of the downstream oil industry entered its first week. (BUSINESSWORLD)
